extracted.intended_audience: general readers of autobiography / readers seeking life-lessons from Andrew Carnegie
extracted.subtask_description: A first-person memoir recounting Andrew Carnegie's childhood, family influences, immigration to America, early work experiences, and formative lessons. The text mixes narrative anecdote with prescriptive observations about upbringing, education, and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of a hero upon children
rubrics_metrics.description: How wonderful is the influence of a hero upon children! 'It is a tower of strength for a boy to have a hero.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carnegie attributes courage and patriotic fervor to identification with heroes (Wallace, Bruce). Example: his childhood imitation of Wallace shaped bravery (walking through the dark Abbey). Use heroes to inspire character and courage in youth; having a hero provides enduring moral and motivational guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraging memorization and recitation in education
rubrics_metrics.description: My good Uncle Lauder justly set great value upon recitation in education... 'I cannot name a more important means of benefiting young people than encouraging them to commit favorite pieces to memory and recite them often.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote memorizing favorite pieces (poems, dialogues) and frequent recitation to strengthen memory, elocution, and confidence. Examples: reciting Norval and Glenalvon, Burns's poems; earned first penny by repeating 'Man was made to Mourn.' Anti-pattern: neglecting oral practice and rote learning of memorable pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement/interest as prerequisite for durable memorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Anything which pleased me I could learn with a rapidity which surprised... I could memorize anything whether it pleased me or not, but if it did not impress me strongly it passed away in a few hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material must be engaging or meaningful to the learner for memorization to stick; select memorable, emotionally resonant content for teaching. Example: favorite poetry stuck, rote-assigned psalms were learned briefly but forgotten later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home-pleasantness as foundational for child development
rubrics_metrics.description: My mother used to say that the first step in this direction was to make home pleasant; and there was nothing she and my father would not do to please us...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pleasant, loving home environment is primary for moral formation and keeping children 'in the right path.' Practical implication: prioritize domestic warmth and attentive parenting as a core educational influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mother as multifaceted educator and moral exemplar
rubrics_metrics.description: The mother, nurse, cook, governess, teacher, saint, all in one; the father, exemplar, guide, counselor, and friend! Thus were my brother and I brought up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value the mother's direct role in teaching language, morals, and practical skills—especially in resource-limited households. Carnegie frames this domestic upbringing as a superior heritage to material wealth. Example: mother binding shoes for income while narrating tales and reciting poetry to children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizing power and ability to choose and lead others
rubrics_metrics.description: I treasure the remembrance of this plan as the earliest evidence of organizing power upon the development of which my material success in life has hung... the faculty of knowing and choosing others who did know better than myself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early evidence of organizing and recruiting others (e.g., arranging rabbit caretakers) is a key predictor of later material success. Guidance: cultivate selection, delegation, and leadership skills; recognize value of choosing competent collaborators. Example: naming rabbits after companions as compensation—rudimentary but instructive organizing act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seize opportunities promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a great mistake not to seize the opportunity... Having got myself in I proposed to stay there if I could.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When offered a chance (job, trial), accept promptly and commit; passivity may forfeit prospects. Example: Carnegie's acceptance of the telegraph messenger trial led to his 'first real start in life.' Anti-pattern: hesitation or refusal to try for fear of inadequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquire practical, market-relevant skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearing that all great firms kept their books in double entry... we all determined to attend night school... and learn the larger system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn concrete skills that local employers value (bookkeeping, penmanship, telegraphy). Practical training (night school) complemented on-the-job duties and opened advancement. Example: moving from steam-engine firing to clerical/bookkeeping tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know people and place (networking and situational knowledge)
rubrics_metrics.description: The next step was to know the men themselves, for it gave a messenger a great advantage... I therefore began to note the signs of these houses up one side of the street and down the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop detailed local knowledge (business names, addresses) and personal acquaintance with people to perform better and gain advantages. Techniques: memorizing street listings, cultivating relationships with employees and employers; outcome: easier, faster message delivery and recognition/compliments from 'great men'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pride, honor, and respectability of character
rubrics_metrics.description: There was not a prouder family in the land. A keen sense of honor, independence, self-respect, pervaded the household... Anything low, mean, deceitful, shifty, coarse, underhand, or gossipy was foreign to that heroic soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instill and maintain personal honor and respectability as a social and moral standard—avoid occupations or associations seen as vagrant or disreputable. Example: mother's fierce rejection of the suggestion that her son become a peddler among 'rough men.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Early industriousness and contribution to family welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: I fairly panted to get to work that I might help the family to a start in the new land... I was now a helper of the family, a breadwinner, and no longer a total charge upon my parents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage early work and responsibility; contributing economically builds self-respect and motivation. Example: first wages in factory and later higher pay at bobbin maker; emotional pride in first week's earnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perseverance and refusal to give up
rubrics_metrics.description: Of one thing I was sure, he ought never to give up... A real disciple of Wallace or Bruce could not give up; he would die first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perseverance in face of discomfort, threat, or hardship is essential. Carnegie frames persistence as an attribute derived from heroic models and national upbringing; practical recommendation: endure unpleasant tasks and conceal struggles from family to maintain honor and contribute.
